name: Example: Computing a Probability Over an Unbounded Interval
problem:
Compute $P\left( X > 8 \right)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14062347/assets/cc8c2867f9ef99a8c476feeb319e03a3a479dd23f04e546bf1e5240daa4ea0ac.png)
worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a <    X <    b) = \int_a^b f(x) \, \textrm dx.
$$

So, in our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>8) & =P(8<X<\infty ) \\  & ={\int }_{8}^{\infty }f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{8}^{\infty }5{e}^{-5x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[-{e}^{-5x}]}_{8}^{\infty } \\  & ={e}^{-40}.\end{aligned}
$$
